name: Hadoram
overview: Hadoram is a male figure mentioned in Scripture as the son of Joktan. Beyond this familial link, there is limited information about his tribe or other distinguishing attributes. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Hadoram means 'Hadad is exalted,' reflecting a theophoric element common in ancient Semitic names. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 10:27 and was not given directly by God but carries a meaning that connects to the exaltation of Hadad.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hadoram as a son of Joktan, establishing his place within a genealogical line. No other family relationships are recorded for him beyond this connection in Genesis 10:27.
scriptureSignificance: Hadoram's significance lies in his role as a descendant of Joktan, situating him within the broader biblical genealogy that traces the post-Flood nations. His mention helps to outline the lineage and tribal divisions that are foundational for understanding the distribution of peoples in the biblical narrative.
